subject: Prepay options & stepdown schedule for Nimbus Labs
messages:
From: Eli Navarro <eli@nimbus.ai>
To: Rachel Kim <rachel_kim@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 30 Jun 2026 10:05:12 -0700
Subject: Prepay options for startup usage

Rachel —

Thanks again for the demo last week. We ran a quick internal model and are trying to figure out whether a 12- or 24-month prepay (with credits) makes sense for us as we scale from pilot to production. High-level:

- Current MRR: ~$6k; expected to grow to ~$45k by month 9 with new feature rollout.
- We care about predictable unit cost while we optimize prompts.

Questions:
1) What kind of term discounts do you offer for 12 vs 24 month prepay?
2) Do you support a step-down minimum (higher upfront, lower trailing minimums) or milestone-based vesting of credits?
3) Any startup-friendly credit tweaks (front-loaded credits, usage forgiveness early months)?

I've attached a one-pager of our usage forecast (Nimbus-forecast-usage.xlsx). Procurement will likely be involved once we land on a number: procurement@nimbus.ai.

Would you have a quick sketch we can iterate on today? We're trying to lock something in before our seed closing.

—Eli
Eli Navarro
Founder & CEO | Nimbus Labs
eli@nimbus.ai

From: Rachel Kim <rachel_kim@redwood.ai>
To: Eli Navarro <eli@nimbus.ai>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 30 Jun 2026 13:28:45 -0700
Subject: Re: Prepay options for startup usage

Eli —

Appreciate the context and the forecast, that helps a lot. Attached is a quick draft (RNW-proposal-draft.pdf) with two clean options and an alternate ramp that often works well for early-stage customers. High level:

Option A — 12 months, moderate prepay- 12 month commitment, $120k prepaid (credit balance)- Effective term discount: 18% vs pay-as-you-go expected run rate- Step-down minima: months 1–3: 40% of committed; months 4–12: 25%- Front-loaded credits: +15% one-time onboarding credits applied to month 1 usage

Option B — 24 months, extended commitment- 24 month commitment, $200k prepaid- Effective term discount: 26% vs pay-as-you-go- Step-down minima: months 1–6: 35%; months 7–24: 20%- Milestone vesting: 25% of credits vest after month 6 if usage targets met

A couple of notes:
- We can be flexible on the step-down schedule; MRPs (minimum ramp percentages) are intended to protect both sides while you're scaling.
- If you prefer, we can do a 12–24 split (pay $120k today, reserve right to top up to $200k at a fixed rate within 6 months) to reduce up-front cash.

If procurement is going to pull in legal, happy to provide standard MOA language. Also happy to jump on a 20-min call to walk through the numbers.

Next steps I propose:
1) You and procurement confirm which option (A/B/Hybrid).
2) We send a version with clear monthly ramp schedule and DocuSign link.

Thanks —
Rachel Kim
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
Rachel_kim@redwood.ai

From: Rachel Kim <rachel_kim@redwood.ai>

Date: Wed, 01 Jul 2026 09:14:02 -0700
Subject: Fwd: Prepay options for startup usage — quick internal alignment

Vivek / Karthik —

Heads-up: Nimbus (small seed startup) is evaluating a 12–24m prepay. Eli pushed a usage forecast and asked for startup-friendly credits. My proposed options are in the attached draft; key considerations:

- Risk profile: higher churn risk but low current spend; they will scale if product-market fit holds.
- Margin impact: Option B (24m) is ~26% effective discount; if we add deeper concession it materially changes unit economics.

Recommendation ask:
1) Approve a one-time promotional credit of +10% on top of Option B if they commit to 24m >= $250k (this can be time-limited).
2) Allow milestone vesting (25% release after month 6) to reduce front-loaded credit exposure.
3) Approve a step-down minimum that starts high (35–40%) but drops to 20% after month 6.

If you approve, I'll share a revised proposal with a clear monthly step-down schedule and a draft MOA for procurement.

—Rachel

From: Eli Navarro <eli@nimbus.ai>
To: Rachel Kim <rachel_kim@redwood.ai>
Cc: procurement@nimbus.ai
Date: Fri, 02 Jul 2026 11:03:19 -0700
Subject: Re: Prepay options for startup usage

Rachel —

Thanks for the clear options. Quick counter + clarifying items from our side:

- We're inclined to Option B but request: an initial credit boost of 20% applied in month 1 (helps absorb early dev spikes).
- Can we agree to a 6-month ramp schedule with specific monthly minima (we proposed: 60%, 50%, 40%, 35%, 30%, 25% for months 1–6 respectively, then 20% thereafter)?
- We'd like an SLA credit in case of >2 outages/month during first 6 months (we're sensitive to latency for pilot users).

Procurement is happy to take the MOA and run it through legal once we have clear numbers.

If you can marginally improve the month-1 credit (20% vs 15), I think we're ready to proceed to signatures.

—Eli

From: Rachel Kim <rachel_kim@redwood.ai>

Subject: RE: Prepay options for startup usage — final confirmation

Eli —

Thanks — we can accommodate the revised terms with a small concession:

Agreed summary (Option B, revised):
- Commitment: 24 months, $200,000 prepay (credit balance).
- Term discount: effective ~24% (after concession).
- Front-loaded credit: 20% one-time onboarding credit in month 1 (applied to usage).
- Monthly minima (months 1–6): 60%, 50%, 40%, 35%, 30%, 25%; months 7–24: 20%.
- Milestone vesting: 25% of the prepay credits unlock after month 6 provided usage target X (see RNW proposal) is met.
- SLA: standard SLA with a 5% monthly credit for qualifying >2 outage events in any 30-day window during first 6 months.

Next steps:
1) Procurement: I'll send a DocuSign MOA (final-signed-MOA.docx will be included).
2) Finance: we'll route invoice as prepay; refunds/adjustments under MOA if milestones not met.
3) Implementation: onboarding kickoff scheduled for week of Jul 12.

Eli, if this matches your expectations reply with a quick "Agree" and I'll route the DocuSign.

Best —
